content: 1. Neomycin and Amikacin/Neomycin and Amphotericin B/Neomycin and Cidofovir/Neomycin and Contrast Media (Iodinated)/Neomycin and Ioversol/Neomycin and Tacrolimus/Neomycin and Teicoplanin/Neomycin and Acyclovir: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity (kidney damage) and/or ototoxicity (hearing damage). These combinations are contraindicated, and alternative therapies should be considered. 2. Neomycin and Atracurium: Neomycin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Neomycin and BCG Vaccine (Live): Neomycin reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 4. Neomycin and Bumetanide/Neomycin and Capreomycin/Neomycin and Cephaloridine: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Neomycin and Cholera Vaccine: Neomycin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine within 14 days of antibiotic use. 6. Neomycin and Cisatracurium/Neomycin and Colistin/Neomycin and Ethacrynic Acid/Neomycin and Furosemide/Neomycin and Gentamicin: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Neomycin and Microbiota Oral: Neomycin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 8. Neomycin and Pancuronium/Neomycin and Polymyxin B: Neomycin enhances the effects of these drugs, increasing the risk of apnea and nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Neomycin and Quinidine: Quinidine increases the levels of neomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Neomycin and Rocuronium/Neomycin and Succinylcholine/Neomycin and Tobramycin/Neomycin and Torsemide: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Neomycin and Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Neomycin reduces the efficacy of the typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 12. Neomycin and Vecuronium: Neomycin enhances the effects of vecuronium, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Neomycin and Adefovir/Neomycin and Amiodarone: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 14. Neomycin and Conjugated Estrogens/Ethinyl Estradiol/Levonorgestrel: Neomycin reduces the levels of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 15. Neomycin and Cyclosporine/Digoxin/Dronedarone: These drugs increase the levels of neomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 16. Neomycin and Foscarnet/Neomycin and Methoxyflurane: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 17. Neomycin and Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Neomycin reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. Use caution and monitor. 18. Neomycin and Warfarin: Neomycin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Neomycin and NSAIDs (e.g., Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Ketorolac): These drugs increase the levels of neomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants. 20. Neomycin and Aztreonam: These drugs may be used synergistically against Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacteriaceae. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Neomycin and Balsalazide/Biotin/Calcium Supplements: Neomycin reduces the levels of these agents by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The significance is unknown. 22. Neomycin and Diclofenac/Diflunisal: These drugs increase the levels of neomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants. 23. Neomycin and Entecavir: These drugs increase each other's effects by decreasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Neomycin and Fluconazole/Ketoconazole: These drugs decrease the levels of neomycin through an unknown mechanism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Neomycin and Magnesium Supplements: Neomycin reduces the levels of magnesium supplements by increasing renal clearance. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Neomycin and Mefenamic Acid/Meloxicam: These drugs increase the levels of neomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and mainly occurs in preterm infants. 27. Neomycin and Vancomycin: These drugs increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 28. Neomycin and Verapamil/Voclosporin: These drugs increase the levels of neomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 29. Neomycin and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases the levels of neomycin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 30. Neomycin and Streptomycin/Streptozocin: These combinations increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 31. Neomycin and Tenofovir DF: Neomycin increases the levels of tenofovir by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor. 32. Neomycin and Trazodone: Trazodone decreases the levels of neomycin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 33. Neomycin and Tolvaptan: Tolvaptan increases the levels of neomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 34. Neomycin and Cordyceps: Cordyceps decreases the toxicity of neomycin through an unspecified mechanism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Neomycin and Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12): Neomycin reduces the levels of cyanocobalamin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The significance is unknown. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when neomycin is coadministered with other drugs to minimize risks of toxicity or reduced efficacy.
